description:
Residual from bedrock-w10's cold review.

With w10, the Director reads the bootstrap once at recovery start (`PersistencePhase.read_bootstrap/1`) but discards the object version token; `PersistencePhase` later does its own `get_with_version` and `put_if_version_matches` at write time. So a Director that started from record R will still overwrite a record written in between by another (older, still-running) Director — the CAS fences against concurrent writers at write time, not against the state this recovery was planned from.

FDB fences here by writing cstate immediately after reading it with `recoveryCount++` (ClusterRecovery.actor.cpp ~1584-1590), so any older recovery's later write fails. Expected: the version read at recovery start is the one the persistence write must match (or an equivalent generation fence). Note the unmerged bedrock-7i1 / bedrock-t0k / bedrock-50n work (PRs #306/#308, reservation + retained CAS token) targets this territory — reconcile rather than duplicate.
title: PersistencePhase overwrites the bootstrap without fencing on the version the recovery started from
